name: @lism-css/mcp

tools.name: get_overview
tools.description:
Get an overview of the lism-css framework: architecture, design philosophy, packages, breakpoints, CSS layers, and implementation rules.
Use this as your FIRST call when starting any lism-css task — it provides the foundational context needed to use other tools effectively.
Do NOT use this to look up specific components (use get_component), individual props (use get_props_system), or design tokens (use get_tokens).
The response is pre-formatted Markdown. Output it verbatim to the user. Do NOT summarize or omit sections.

tools.name: get_tokens
tools.description:
Get design tokens (colors, spacing, font sizes, shadows, etc.) used in lism-css. Returns the full token reference including CSS variable names and available values.
Use this when you need to check available token values, variable names, or design scales (e.g. "what spacing values exist?", "what are the font size tokens?").
For prop-to-CSS mappings, get_props_system is more suitable. For CSS conversion, use convert_css. Call get_overview first if you have not yet.
The response is pre-formatted Markdown. Output it verbatim. Do NOT summarize or omit token values.

tools.name: get_props_system
tools.description:
Get the lism-css Props system reference: how React/Astro props map to CSS classes and styles. Supports lookup by lism prop name (e.g. "p", "fz") OR by CSS property name (e.g. "padding", "font-size"). Omit the prop parameter to get the full reference.
Use this when you need to find a specific prop mapping, understand the Property Class system, or check what CSS property a lism prop corresponds to.
For bulk CSS-to-lism conversion, convert_css is more efficient. For component-specific documentation, use get_component.
The response is pre-formatted Markdown. Output it verbatim. Do NOT summarize the prop tables.

prop.description: Prop name or CSS property name to look up. Accepts lism prop names (e.g. "p", "fz", "bgc") and standard CSS property names (e.g. "padding", "font-size", "background-color"). Omit to get the full reference.

tools.name: get_component
tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific lism-css component: purpose, props, and usage examples.
Use this when you need documentation for a known component by name (e.g. "Box", "Flex", "Accordion", "Lism", "HTML").
Accepts multiple notations: "Flex", "<Flex>", "l--flex", "flex" all resolve to the same entry.
Do NOT use this for broad topic guides (use get_guide with "components-core" or "components-ui") or keyword search across all docs (use search_docs).
If the component is not found, suggestions will be provided — follow up with search_docs for a broader query.
The response is pre-formatted Markdown. Output it verbatim. Do NOT summarize or omit code examples.

package.description: Filter by package. "lism-css" for core components, "@lism-css/ui" for UI components.

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description:
Get a detailed guide on a specific lism-css topic. Use this when you need comprehensive documentation on a broad topic rather than a specific component or prop.
For individual component lookup, get_component is more direct. For individual prop lookup, use get_props_system.
The response is the full guide as pre-formatted Markdown. Output it verbatim. Do NOT summarize or omit sections.

Available topics:
- overview: Framework overview, packages, implementation rules
- tokens: Design tokens (spacing, colors, font sizes, etc.)
- property-class: Property Class system, all props reference table, border (bd) / hover (hov) / max-sz details
- components-core: Core component system (Lism, Box, Flex, Stack, Grid, etc.)
- components-ui: UI components (Accordion, Modal, Tabs, Button, etc.)
- base-styles: Base styling, reset CSS, HTML element styles
- set-class: Set classes (set--plain, set--bxsh, set--hov, etc.)
- primitive-class: Primitive class prefixes (l--, a--), with column-layout primitive selection guide
- trait-class: Trait classes (is--, has--): declarative role/feature classes in the lism-trait layer
- utility-class: Utility classes (u--trim, u--cbox, etc.)
- css-rules: CSS methodology, layer structure, Block Class (b--) / Custom Class (c--), naming conventions
- naming: Naming conventions: CSS variable / class naming rules, {prop} and {value} abbreviation rules
- responsive: Responsive design, breakpoints, container queries
- customize: Customization: @layer opt-out, SCSS settings, lism.config.js, CSS purge
- antipatterns: AI code-generation antipatterns (values / style declarations): px hardcoding, token typos, keycolor misuse, prop type mistakes
- antipatterns-layout: AI code-generation antipatterns (structure / layout / responsive): layout choice errors, responsive omissions, is-- misuse, naming mistakes

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description:
Search lism-css documentation by keyword. Returns matching pages with relevance scores. Supports CSS property names (e.g. 'font-size', 'padding') which are automatically expanded to corresponding lism prop names.
Use this when you cannot find information with other tools, or to discover available components, features, and guides by keyword.
Do NOT use this as your first step — prefer get_component for a known component, get_props_system for a known prop, or get_guide for a specific topic. This is a fallback search tool.
Returns JSON with search results including page URLs and relevance scores. Each result includes a nextTool field with the recommended follow-up tool call for fetching that page in detail.

query.description: Search query (keywords separated by spaces). CSS property names like "font-size" are also accepted.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: convert_css
tools.description:
Convert CSS code to lism-css props, utility classes, and component suggestions. Accepts CSS declarations (with or without selectors) and returns the equivalent lism-css representation as structured JSON.
Use this when migrating existing CSS to lism-css in bulk, or when you need to understand how multiple CSS properties map to lism-css at once.
Do NOT use this for single prop lookups (use get_props_system instead). Note: @media and other at-rules are NOT supported — an error will be returned if detected.
Returns JSON with conversions (prop mappings with confidence), component suggestions, and a JSX usage example.

css.description: CSS code to convert. Accepts a full rule block with selector (e.g. ".foo { padding: 1rem; }") or bare declarations (e.g. "padding: 1rem; font-size: 16px;"). @media and other at-rules are not supported.

instructions: Documentation server for the Lism CSS framework (lism-css). Recommended workflow: call get_overview FIRST to load foundational context, then use get_component for a known component, get_props_system for a known prop or CSS property, or get_guide for a broad topic. Use search_docs only as a fallback keyword search when other tools do not cover the need. Use convert_css to migrate existing CSS to Lism props in bulk. All tools are read-only. Guide content is written in Japanese.
